summary: When a house and the floor above it, owned by two people, fall down, the owners share the wood, stones and earth. Whoever recognizes some of his own stones takes them as part of his share.

chunks.en: If a house and its upper floor, owned by two people, fell down,
chunks.st: In the case of the house and the upper story belonging to two people, i.e., the lower story was owned by one individual, while the upper story belonged to someone else, that collapsed,

chunks.en: both of them share the wood, the stones and the earth.
chunks.st: the two of them divide the timber and the stones and the earth of the collapsed structure.

chunks.en: And we look at which stones were likely to break.
chunks.explain: Those likely belonged to the one whose floor broke them.
chunks.st: And the court considers which stones were likely to break,
chunks.stMore: those of the lower or upper story, and gives those broken stones to the one who presumably owned them.

chunks.en: If one of them
chunks.st: If one of them

chunks.en: recognizes some of his stones,
chunks.st: recognized some of his stones

chunks.en: he takes them, and they count as part of his share.
chunks.st: he may take them for himself, and they count toward his amount
chunks.stMore: of stones, and the other party takes other stones accordingly. They do not divide the remaining stones equally.

summary: If the upper floor that someone rents breaks and the owner will not fix it, the renter may live downstairs until it is fixed. Rabbi Yosei teaches who pays for which part of a broken ceiling.

chunks.en: A house and an upper floor of two people:
chunks.st: If there was a house and an upper story owned by one person, and the upper story was rented out to another,

chunks.en: the upper floor broke,
chunks.st: if the floor of the upper story was broken, i.e., it fell in or collapsed,

chunks.en: and the owner of the house does not want to fix it,
chunks.st: and the owner of the house does not want to repair it,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי בַעַל הָעֲלִיָּה יוֹרֵד וְדָר לְמַטָּה,
chunks.en: the one upstairs goes down and lives below
chunks.st: the resident of the upper story can go down and live in the house below

chunks.en: until he fixes the upper floor for him.
chunks.st: until the owner repairs the upper story for him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:
chunks.stMore: With regard to a house of two stories owned by two people, i.e., the lower level was owned by one and the upper level by the other, in which the ceiling collapsed;

chunks.en: the one below gives the ceiling,
chunks.explain: The beams that hold up the floor.
chunks.st: the owner of the lower story provides the ceiling of beams or stones,

chunks.en: and the one above gives the plaster.
chunks.st: and the owner of the upper story provides the plaster.

summary: When a two-story house owned by two people falls and the lower owner will not rebuild, the upper owner may rebuild and live there until he is paid back. Rabbi Yehuda says he must build both floors so he is not living for free.

chunks.en: If a house and its upper floor, owned by two people, fell down,
chunks.st: In the case of the house and the upper story belonging to two different people, and that house and upper story collapsed,

chunks.he: אָמַר בַּעַל הָעֲלִיָּה לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת לִבְנוֹת,
chunks.en: and the upper owner told the house owner to build,
chunks.st: and the owner of the upper story told the owner of the house to build the lower story in order to enable him to rebuild the upper story,

chunks.en: and he does not want to build,
chunks.st: and he does not want to build it,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי בַעַל הָעֲלִיָּה בּוֹנֶה אֶת הַבַּיִת
chunks.en: the upper owner may build the house
chunks.st: the owner of the upper story may build the house

chunks.en: and live in it
chunks.st: and reside in it,

chunks.en: until he pays him back what he spent.
chunks.st: until the other gives him his expenses
chunks.stMore: for the construction of the house, and he then rebuilds his upper story.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אַף זֶה דָּר בְּתוֹךְ שֶׁל חֲבֵרוֹ,
chunks.en: "But then he lives in his friend's place,
chunks.st: This one too, i.e., the owner of the upper story, who is meanwhile residing inside the property of the other,

chunks.en: and he would have to pay him rent.
chunks.st: must pay him rent.
chunks.stMore: Since he derived benefit by living in the house of the other, as he had no other place in which he could live, he must pay rent. This solution is therefore flawed.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא בַעַל הָעֲלִיָּה בּוֹנֶה אֶת הַבַּיִת
chunks.en: Rather, the upper owner builds the house
chunks.st: Rather, the owner of the upper story builds the house

chunks.en: and the upper floor, and puts the roof on the upper floor,
chunks.st: and the upper story, and he roofs the upper story, i.e., he completes the entire construction of the upper story,

chunks.en: and lives in the house
chunks.st: and he may then sit in the house, i.e., the lower story,

chunks.en: until he pays him back what he spent."
chunks.explain: He could live upstairs, so living below is not a gain for him.
chunks.st: until the other gives him his expenses
chunks.stMore: for the building of the house, at which point he returns to his upper story. Since in any event he could have lived in the upper story, he is not considered to have derived any benefit by living in the lower story, and is not obligated to pay rent.

summary: If a garden on the roof of an olive press falls in, the garden owner may plant below until the roof is fixed. An owner does not pay for damage from a falling wall or tree unless beis din told him to take it down and he waited too long.

chunks.he: וְכֵן בֵּית הַבַּד שֶׁהוּא בָנוּי בְּסֶלַע,
chunks.en: And the same with an olive press built in a rock,
chunks.st: And likewise, in the case of an olive press that is built inside a cave in a rock,

chunks.en: with a garden on top of it,
chunks.st: and one garden, belonging to another person, was planted on top of it,

chunks.he: וְנִפְחַת, הֲרֵי בַעַל הַגִּנָּה יוֹרֵד וְזוֹרֵעַ לְמַטָּה
chunks.en: and it broke through, the garden owner goes down and plants below
chunks.st: and the roof of the olive press broke, which caused the garden to collapse inward, in such a case, the owner of the garden may descend and sow below

chunks.en: until the other makes arches for his olive press.
chunks.explain: Strong arches to hold up the roof.
chunks.st: until the other one constructs for his olive press sturdy arches
chunks.stMore: to support the roof, so that the owner of the garden can once again sow above him. The mishna continues:

chunks.he: הַכֹּתֶל וְהָאִילָן שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים וְהִזִּיקוּ,
chunks.en: A wall or a tree that fell into a public place and did damage,
chunks.st: In the case of a wall or a tree that fell into the public domain and caused damage,

chunks.en: he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: the owner is exempt from having to pay, as it was an accident.

chunks.en: If they gave him time
chunks.st: If the court saw that the wall was shaky, or that the tree was tilting, and they gave him time

chunks.he: לָקֹץ אֶת הָאִילָן וְלִסְתֹּר אֶת הַכֹּתֶל,
chunks.en: to cut down the tree or knock down the wall,
chunks.st: to cut down the tree or to dismantle the wall,

chunks.en: and they fell within the time, he does not pay;
chunks.st: and then they fell down, if this occurred during the allotted time, he is exempt,

chunks.en: after the time, he must pay.
chunks.st: but if they collapsed after the time given to him had elapsed, he is liable to pay, since he was warned against this very occurrence.

summary: Once someone takes on stones or straw instead of his pay, the other cannot take it back. Things like manure, clay and building stones may stay in a public place only a short time, and whoever leaves them there pays for damage.

chunks.en: If someone's wall was next to
chunks.st: In the case of one whose wall was adjacent to another’s garden,

chunks.en: his friend's garden and it fell,
chunks.st: and the wall fell,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "Clear away your stones,"
chunks.st: and the owner of the garden said to him: Clear away your stones,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "They are yours now,"
chunks.st: and the owner of the stones said to him: They are yours,
chunks.stMore: as I hereby declare them ownerless, and you can take them for yourself;

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.explain: He cannot force the other to take them.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him, since he cannot force the other to acquire the stones.

chunks.en: Once the garden owner took them,
chunks.st: If after the owner of the garden voluntarily accepted ownership of the stones upon himself,

chunks.en: if he says to him, "Here are your costs,
chunks.st: the owner of the wall said to him: Here you are, take your expenditures for the removal of the stones,

chunks.en: and I will take mine,"
chunks.st: and I will take the stones that are mine;

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him,
chunks.stMore: as they had already been acquired by the owner of the garden. The mishna continues:

chunks.en: If someone hires a worker
chunks.st: In the case of one who hires a laborer

chunks.en: to work with him with hay and straw,
chunks.st: to do work with him with hay or with straw, and after he finished the task,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "Give me my pay,"
chunks.st: the laborer said to the employer: Give me my wages, and

chunks.he: וְאָמַר לוֹ טֹל מַה שֶּׁעָשִׂיתָ בִּשְׂכָרֶךָ,
chunks.en: and he said to him, "Take what you worked on as your pay,"
chunks.st: the employer said to him: Take what you have worked with as your wages, i.e., take some of the hay or straw as payment,

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.explain: He must pay what they agreed.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him.
chunks.stMore: Although debts can be paid with any item of value, even hay or straw, the wages of a laborer must be paid in accordance with the initial agreement between the laborer and the employer.

chunks.en: Once the worker agreed,
chunks.st: But if after the laborer accepted upon himself to keep the hay or straw as payment, the employer changed his mind

chunks.en: if he says to him, "Here is your pay,
chunks.st: and said to him: Here you are, take your wages

chunks.en: and I will take mine,"
chunks.st: and I will take what is mine;

chunks.en: we do not listen to him.
chunks.st: the court does not listen to him, since the laborer had already acquired the hay.

chunks.en: If someone takes manure out to a public place,
chunks.st: In the case of one who takes manure out to the public domain, in order for it to be transported to fertilize a field,

chunks.en: the one who takes it out does so, and the one who spreads it does so right away.
chunks.explain: It may not sit in the street.
chunks.st: he who takes it out from his property takes it out, and immediately, he who takes it to fertilize the field takes it to fertilize
chunks.stMore: the field. They must relocate the manure immediately without allowing it to sit around in the public domain.

chunks.en: We may not soak clay in a public place,
chunks.st: Similarly, one may not soak clay in the public domain before it is kneaded,

chunks.en: and we may not make bricks there.
chunks.st: and one may not mold bricks
chunks.stMore: in the public domain since this takes a long time and inhibits use of the public domain by others.

chunks.en: But we may knead clay in a public place,
chunks.st: But one may knead clay in the public domain, as this process does not take long,

chunks.en: but not bricks.
chunks.st: but not bricks.

chunks.en: One who builds in a public place:
chunks.st: With regard to one who builds a structure, keeping the building materials in the public domain,

chunks.en: the one who brings stones brings them, and the builder builds right away.
chunks.st: he who brings the stones brings them, and immediately, he who builds the structure builds with them, and may not leave them there.

chunks.en: And if it did damage,
chunks.st: And if the stones cause damage before he had a chance to build them into the structure,

chunks.en: he pays for the damage.
chunks.st: he must pay for what he damaged.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: he may even get his work ready
chunks.st: One may even prepare his work

chunks.en: thirty days before.
chunks.st: thirty days beforehand;
chunks.stMore: he may keep the building materials in the public domain for that duration.

summary: Vegetables grew in the wall of earth between an upper garden and a lower garden. Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon argue about who owns them.

chunks.he: שְׁתֵּי גִנּוֹת זוֹ עַל גַּב זוֹ
chunks.en: Two gardens, one above the other,
chunks.st: In the case of two gardens that were located one above the other, i.e., a garden on a plateau that borders another garden below,

chunks.en: and vegetables in between.
chunks.explain: They grew out of the wall of earth between them.
chunks.st: and vegetables grew in-between,
chunks.stMore: out of the wall of soil resulting from the difference in height between the two gardens,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: they belong to the upper one.
chunks.st: These vegetables belong to the owner of the upper garden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: they belong to the lower one.
chunks.st: They belong to the owner of the lower one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said in explanation of his ruling:

chunks.he: אִם יִרְצֶה הָעֶלְיוֹן לִקַּח אֶת עֲפָרוֹ
chunks.en: "If the upper one wants to take away his earth,
chunks.st: If the owner of the upper garden would want to dig and take his dirt and does so,

chunks.en: there are no vegetables here."
chunks.st: no vegetables would grow here,
chunks.stMore: as that wall made of soil would not exist. The vegetables therefore belong to him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda said,
chunks.st: In response, Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.he: אִם יִרְצֶה הַתַּחְתּוֹן לְמַלְּאוֹת אֶת גִּנָּתוֹ
chunks.en: "If the lower one wants to fill his garden,
chunks.st: If the owner of the lower garden would want to fill his garden with dirt and does so, thereby raising its level,

chunks.en: there are no vegetables here."
chunks.st: no vegetables would grow here,
chunks.stMore: as that wall made of soil would not exist. The vegetables therefore belong to him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.en: "Since both of them can stop
chunks.st: Since the two of them can object

chunks.en: each other,
chunks.st: to each other,
chunks.stMore: as they each have the ability to prevent the vegetable growth, nothing can be decided based on such considerations.

chunks.en: we look at where these vegetables get their life from."
chunks.st: Instead, the court considers from where this vegetable lives and derives nourishment, whether from above or from below.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.en: "Whatever the upper one can reach out
chunks.st: Any vegetables that the owner of the upper garden

chunks.en: his hand and take
chunks.st: can stretch out his hand and take,

chunks.en: is his,
chunks.st: those vegetables are his,

chunks.en: and the rest belongs to the lower one."
chunks.st: and the rest belong to the owner of the lower garden.
